result.rationale: refreshOAuthTokens returns a raw fetch Response when credential sync is enabled (`const response = await fetch(...); return response;`), but googlecalendar's CalendarService does `const res = await refreshOAuthTokens(...); const token = res?.data;` — a fetch Response has no `data` property, so token is undefined and `token.access_token` throws, crashing the refresh flow in sync mode.

judged_text: When credential sync is enabled, refreshOAuthTokens returns a raw fetch Response object, and the code then reads `res?.data` — a property that does not exist on a fetch Response — so token is undefined. `token.access_token` throws TypeError (Cannot read properties of undefined) inside refreshAccessToken, turning a refresh under credential-sharing mode into an unhandled 500 on the booking path instead of a token refresh.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts`, when `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED && process.env.CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT && userId`, it performs `fetch(...)` and returns that raw `Response` object. But callers (e.g. `packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts`) treat the return value like an axios/google client response: `const res = await refreshOAuthTokens(...); const token = res?.data;` and then use `token.access_token`. A `fetch` `Response` has no `.data`, so `token` becomes `undefined` and `token.access_token` will throw at runtime when credential sync mode is enabled.
